Terms:

Ambush Geometry - The arrangement of terrain and positioning used to maximize the effectiveness of an ambush.

Blacked-out Headlights - Vehicle headlights turned off for stealth during night operations.

Civilian Friction - Situations involving civilians that create moral and operational dilemmas.

Command Track - A system to track oversight, scrutiny, and political tolerance.

Daisy-Chained IEDs - Multiple explosive devices connected together to detonate simultaneously or sequentially.

Friction Relief Conditions - Conditions under which operational friction can be reduced.

Herding Ambush - A tactic where the enemy manipulates movement to drive a patrol into a prepared ambush.

Quiet Success - A mission outcome with no contact, no civilian harm, and no compromise.

Sunlight Clock - A solo play pacing mechanism that tracks time, adjust pressure, and visibility during the mission.

Tactical Feint - A deceptive maneuver to mislead the enemy.

Timeline Pressure - The stress caused by time constraints during a mission.

Withdrawal - A deliberate decision to retreat from an enemy under constraint.
